For the Hegotá agenda: EIP-8198 (Quick Slots) now has an upstream-facing executable EL implementation of the schedule-driven direction.

- execution-specs PR: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3473
- EIP-side SLOT_SCHEDULE proposal: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11458
- current validated head: `f06d972f496ca9325559f840db45a10cfd6f86e1`
- Amsterdam base: `6eb68ed3e611a25c8d96292ec61e0aee37f894b4`
- exact validation: https://github.com/chugarchugarr/execution-specs/actions/runs/33451124564

The implementation preserves the current Hegotá-facing behavior while using synthetic later duration eras only to prove that the same production paths compose without new duration-specific EL branches.

The narrow question I would like resolved during EIP-8198 discussion is: should the EL side also pay the refactor cost once so later slot-duration reductions become schedule/config changes rather than new transition-specific execution logic?
